tools.name: get_my_tasks
tools.description: Read the authenticated user's own task list. Returns a small page of tasks.

tools.name: get_my_goals
tools.description: Read the authenticated user's own goals and milestone counts.

tools.name: get_my_context
tools.description: Read what the authenticated user wrote about themselves in Settings → My Context: their work, routines, preferences and how they like advice given, in their own words, plus the name they want to be called. Use it to personalize suggestions. It is the user's description, not a record of what they did, and it may be empty.

tools.name: get_my_habits
tools.description: Read active habits and recent streak/completion summaries belonging to the authenticated user.

tools.name: get_my_calendar
tools.description: Read the user's calendar and availability in the user's timezone. Defaults to today and the next 6 days. The range is limited to 14 days.

tools.name: get_daily_overview
tools.description: Read the authenticated user's whole day: their routine (wake, bed, work hours, focus length), today's timed schedule, the tasks due, planned, overdue, completed and coming up, active goals with progress and next milestone, and habits with today's check-in and streak. Times are already on the user's clock. Use it for questions about today, the user's routine or plan.

tools.name: get_daily_review
tools.description: Read a date-specific LifestyleOS review for the authenticated user, including distinct planned/completed tasks, status cycles, schedule history, and transparent time-tracking availability. Use this for Daily Review requests. Never change tasks based on this data.

reviewDate.description: Optional local date YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today in the user's timezone.

tools.name: get_task_priorities
tools.description: Read Michael's suggested order for the user's open tasks: each task's rank, a 0–100 score and the components behind it (their priority, due date, goal links, effort against time left, past postponements). The order is computed by a published deterministic formula, not by you: explain it using the reasons and numbers given, never compute or invent a score. It changes nothing; the user overrides it by changing a task's priority, due date or goal links.

tools.name: get_project_delivery_risk
tools.description: Read the computed delivery risk score, every weighted input behind it, and the throughput forecast for one project in the authorized organization. All figures are already calculated; report them exactly as given and never recompute, combine or estimate any number. Organization identity is selected and authorized by the server, not a tool argument.

projectId.description: The project to read risk for, within the already-authorized organization.

tools.name: get_project_execution_metrics
tools.description: Read completion metrics for one project and each of its milestones, including completion by task count and by estimate with estimate coverage. Figures are already calculated; never recompute or re-derive them.

projectId.description: The project to read metrics for, within the already-authorized organization.

tools.name: get_task_dependency_analysis
tools.description: Read why one work task is blocked: its unmet blockers, longest dependency chain, critical path and downstream impact. A blocker the caller may not see is counted but reported without identity. Figures are already calculated; never recompute them.

taskId.description: The work task to analyse, within the already-authorized organization.

tools.name: get_work_task_priorities
tools.description: Read Michael's suggested order for open work tasks the user can see: each task's rank, a 0–100 score and the components behind it (priority, due date, project priority and target, how many open tasks wait on it, effort against time left), and whether it is waiting on an unfinished task. The order is computed by a published deterministic formula, not by you: explain it using the reasons and numbers given, never compute or invent a score. It changes nothing. Organization identity is selected and authorized by the server, not a tool argument.

scope.description: mine: tasks assigned to the user (default). visible: every open task the user can see.

tools.name: find_projects
tools.description: Find projects the user can see in the authorized organization, by name. Returns each project's id, name, status, priority and dates; use the id with the project risk and metrics tools. Organization identity is selected and authorized by the server, not a tool argument.

search.description: Part of the project name to look for. Leave empty to list the most recently updated projects.

tools.name: find_work_tasks
tools.description: Find work tasks the user can see in the authorized organization. search matches task titles only, never project names: to list a project's tasks, first call find_projects and pass its id as projectId. Returns each task's id, title, status, priority, due date and project; use the id with the dependency analysis tool. Organization identity is selected and authorized by the server, not a tool argument.

search.description: Part of a task title to look for. Leave empty to list tasks by due date, or when filtering by projectId.

projectId.description: Only tasks in this project: its id from find_projects, or its exact name.

tools.name: get_organization_overview
tools.description: Read safe summary details for the currently authorized WorkOS organization. Organization identity is selected and authorized by the server, not a tool argument.

tools.name: get_organization_members
tools.description: List organization directory details only when the authenticated user's current organization permission allows it.

tools.name: draft_task
tools.description: Prepare an unsaved task for the user to review and save. This does NOT save anything and creates no record. Pass only details the user actually gave; omit anything they did not say rather than inventing it. The reply tells you which required details are still missing so you can ask for them. After calling this, tell the user the draft is below and that they must press Save.

title.description: What the task is, in the user's own words

priority.description: Only if the user indicated urgency

dueDate.description: Local date YYYY-MM-DD, only if the user gave a date

estimatedDurationMinutes.description: Whole minutes, 5 to 1440, only if the user said how long

tools.name: draft_goal
tools.description: Prepare an unsaved goal for the user to review and save. This does NOT save anything and creates no record. Pass only details the user actually gave. The reply names any required detail still missing. After calling this, tell the user the draft is below and that they must press Save.

title.description: What the user wants to achieve

category.description: Only if the user named an area such as health or career

targetDate.description: Local date YYYY-MM-DD, only if the user gave one

progress.description: Percent 0 to 100, only if the user said they have already started

tools.name: draft_habit
tools.description: Prepare an unsaved habit for the user to review and save. This does NOT save anything and creates no record. Use frequency DAILY for every day, or SELECTED_DAYS with weekdays as ISO numbers where 1 is Monday and 7 is Sunday. If the user said when it happens, pass startTime (and endTime for a span) as 24-hour HH:mm exactly as they said it — 'sleep by 1 AM and wake at 8 AM' is startTime 01:00 and endTime 08:00; 'walk at 7 in the morning' is startTime 07:00. Pass only what the user gave. After calling this, tell the user the draft is below and that they must press Save.

title.description: The habit the user wants to build

weekdays.description: ISO weekdays 1-7, required only when frequency is SELECTED_DAYS

startTime.description: Local start time HH:mm, 24-hour, only if the user said a time

endTime.description: Local end time HH:mm, 24-hour, only if the user gave an end; may be earlier than the start when it runs past midnight

tools.name: draft_calendar_event
tools.description: Prepare an unsaved calendar event for the user to review and save. This does NOT save anything, does NOT change the calendar and creates no record. Give the local date and local start and end times; the user's timezone is applied by the server. Use COMMITMENT for something the user is doing and UNAVAILABLE for time they are not available. To schedule existing tasks across several days, use prepare_schedule_proposal instead. After calling this, tell the user the draft is below and that they must press Save.

endTime.description: Local end time HH:mm, 24-hour, after the start time

tools.name: prepare_schedule_proposal
tools.description: Ask the existing deterministic planner to prepare a reviewable schedule draft for a requested local date range. This does not change the calendar; the user must explicitly approve selected sessions.

fromDate.description: First local date, YYYY-MM-DD, today or later

toDate.description: Last local date, YYYY-MM-DD; up to 7 dates total
